title: Engineering Evolution Framework
purpose: A shared, evidence-led framework for architecture, modernization, verification and operational evolution, including the 20 coordinated implementation directives used across the Ivan-VHS repositories.

adoption.rule: A practice is implemented only when repository-specific code, tests or operational evidence support the claim. Not every practice is appropriate for every repository.

pillars.intent: Define stable module boundaries and versioned contracts. Quantization states precision and error budgets; telemetry is low-cardinality, privacy-conscious and local by default.

practices.guidance: Define stable module boundaries and versioned contracts.
Quantization states precision and error budgets; telemetry is low-cardinality, privacy-conscious and local by default.

acceptance: Quantized values retain units, precision and a documented error bound.
Telemetry records source, time window and sampling policy without exporting secrets.

pillars.intent: Treat events and triggers as explicit inputs. Modernize incrementally against a recorded baseline and calibrate thresholds with representative fixtures.

practices.guidance: Treat events and triggers as explicit inputs.
Modernize incrementally against a recorded baseline and calibrate thresholds with representative fixtures.

acceptance: Behavior-changing work has a before/after baseline and rollback point.
Calibration fixtures cover nominal, boundary and failure conditions.

pillars.intent: Keep canonical state stable. Apply vectorized paths only when they preserve scalar semantics; discretize continuous values with explicit sampling and resolution rules.

practices.guidance: Keep canonical state stable.
Apply vectorized paths only when they preserve scalar semantics; discretize continuous values with explicit sampling and resolution rules.

acceptance: Optimized paths are checked against a trusted scalar/reference implementation.
Sampling intervals, resolution and rounding risks are documented where relevant.

pillars.intent: Make transformations repeatable and isolated behind owned interfaces. Automation is idempotent and least-privileged; encapsulation protects invariants.

practices.guidance: Make transformations repeatable and isolated behind owned interfaces.
Automation is idempotent and least-privileged; encapsulation protects invariants.

acceptance: Repeated automation does not create duplicate or destructive side effects.
Mutable state and transformation preconditions are exposed through validated interfaces.

pillars.intent: Model feature, data and release lifecycles as controlled stages. Parameterize behavior with validated configuration and versioned migration paths.

practices.guidance: Model feature, data and release lifecycles as controlled stages.
Parameterize behavior with validated configuration and versioned migration paths.

acceptance: Lifecycle states and transition rules are documented and testable.
Parameters have schema, units, bounds, defaults and compatibility rules.

pillars.intent: Integrate through explicit adapters and versioned interfaces. Optimize measured bottlenecks; deduplicate work without erasing provenance, ordering or meaningful distinctions.

practices.guidance: Integrate through explicit adapters and versioned interfaces.
Optimize measured bottlenecks; deduplicate work without erasing provenance, ordering or meaningful distinctions.

acceptance: Every integration has an owner, contract and failure mode.
Optimization preserves output semantics and has regression coverage.

pillars.intent: Prefer bounded algorithms with stated complexity. Compilation and packaging are reproducible; containers remain optional tools, not a universal dependency.

practices.guidance: Prefer bounded algorithms with stated complexity.
Compilation and packaging are reproducible; containers remain optional tools, not a universal dependency.

acceptance: Algorithmic limits and worst-case input sizes are declared and tested.
Build inputs and packaged runtime dependencies are traceable.

pillars.intent: Model mechanisms before implementing them. Replicate state or work only under an explicit consistency model, with deterministic fixtures and clear ownership.

practices.guidance: Model mechanisms before implementing them.
Replicate state or work only under an explicit consistency model, with deterministic fixtures and clear ownership.

acceptance: Models define states, transitions, assumptions and failure cases.
Replicas cannot silently diverge or duplicate side effects.

pillars.intent: Evolve systems through versioned configuration and explicit routing rules. Routing is deterministic, observable and allow-listed.

practices.guidance: Evolve systems through versioned configuration and explicit routing rules.
Routing is deterministic, observable and allow-listed.

acceptance: Configuration is validated before activation and has safe defaults.
Destinations and fallback behavior are explicit and tested.

pillars.intent: Separate coupled responsibilities and isolate hot paths. Treat decompression as untrusted input processing with strict size, ratio, path and time limits.

practices.guidance: Separate coupled responsibilities and isolate hot paths.
Treat decompression as untrusted input processing with strict size, ratio, path and time limits.

acceptance: Components have explicit inputs, outputs and resource budgets.
Compressed inputs cannot escape approved output roots.

pillars.intent: Plan capacity against measured demand and declared budgets. Translate formats, units or protocol versions through explicit adapters.

practices.guidance: Plan capacity against measured demand and declared budgets.
Translate formats, units or protocol versions through explicit adapters.

acceptance: Scaling thresholds derive from measurements and resource limits.
Translations preserve units and semantics and report unsupported fields.

pillars.intent: Compose cohesive components with clear lifecycle ownership. Orchestration coordinates; segmentation isolates data, workloads and failure domains.

practices.guidance: Compose cohesive components with clear lifecycle ownership.
Orchestration coordinates; segmentation isolates data, workloads and failure domains.

acceptance: Each component has a clear responsibility and bounded dependencies.
Cancellation, partial failure and segment boundaries are handled explicitly.

pillars.intent: Make capabilities and data flows discoverable. Interpretation explains malformed or ambiguous inputs; aggregation preserves provenance and deterministic ordering.

practices.guidance: Make capabilities and data flows discoverable.
Interpretation explains malformed or ambiguous inputs; aggregation preserves provenance and deterministic ordering.

acceptance: Supported routes and capability boundaries are discoverable.
Aggregated outputs retain source identity, timestamps and conflict information.

pillars.intent: Define consistency and ordering before synchronizing state. Adapt interfaces compatibly; fragment large payloads with integrity checks and explicit reassembly rules.

practices.guidance: Define consistency and ordering before synchronizing state.
Adapt interfaces compatibly; fragment large payloads with integrity checks and explicit reassembly rules.

acceptance: Concurrent updates have a documented conflict and ordering policy.
Fragments are bounded and reassembled without silent truncation.

pillars.intent: Treat safety, data integrity and resource constraints as non-negotiable. Stabilize with timeouts and bounded retries; deploy with health checks and rollback.

practices.guidance: Treat safety, data integrity and resource constraints as non-negotiable.
Stabilize with timeouts and bounded retries; deploy with health checks and rollback.

acceptance: Failure handling avoids infinite retries and unsafe partial state.
Deployments have health gates, rollback paths and approval for privileged changes.

pillars.intent: Specify wire and internal protocols. Reconstruct state only from verifiable evidence; refactor behind compatibility tests while preserving behavior.

practices.guidance: Specify wire and internal protocols.
Reconstruct state only from verifiable evidence; refactor behind compatibility tests while preserving behavior.

acceptance: Protocol versions, error codes and compatibility expectations are documented.
Refactors pass behavioral parity tests and never infer missing source data.

pillars.intent: Use precise structural models for relationships, dimensions and coordinate systems. Verify invariants at boundaries; abstract only when it clarifies contracts.

practices.guidance: Use precise structural models for relationships, dimensions and coordinate systems.
Verify invariants at boundaries; abstract only when it clarifies contracts.

acceptance: Dimensions, units, indices and coordinate assumptions are explicit.
Abstractions have invariant tests and avoid needless indirection.

pillars.intent: Make generators deterministic when seeded and validate artifacts. Use decompilation for read-only inspection; index content with freshness and privacy boundaries.

practices.guidance: Make generators deterministic when seeded and validate artifacts.
Use decompilation for read-only inspection; index content with freshness and privacy boundaries.

acceptance: Generated outputs are reproducible or declare nondeterministic inputs.
Inspection never executes the artifact, and indexes are rebuildable.

pillars.intent: Track changes through measurable milestones. Synthesize sources with explicit conflict handling; serialize stable, versioned representations.

practices.guidance: Track changes through measurable milestones.
Synthesize sources with explicit conflict handling; serialize stable, versioned representations.

acceptance: Milestones have evidence-based exit criteria and measurable outcomes.
Serialized formats are versioned, validated and stable under repeat runs.

pillars.intent: Use historical evidence to forecast capacity, risk and maintenance needs while exposing uncertainty. Deserialize only bounded, schema-validated input.

practices.guidance: Use historical evidence to forecast capacity, risk and maintenance needs while exposing uncertainty.
Deserialize only bounded, schema-validated input.

acceptance: Forecasts state data window, assumptions, confidence and known gaps.
Deserialization rejects oversized, malformed and out-of-range fields safely.

guardrails: Keep project-contract.json and existing architecture and safety contracts authoritative; this framework complements rather than replaces them.
Never mark a capability implemented without repository-specific code, tests or operational evidence.
Prefer existing toolchains; do not introduce a framework, service or container runtime solely to satisfy a vocabulary item.
Keep telemetry local by default, minimize collection, redact secrets and identifiers, and require explicit opt-in before external transmission.
Bound untrusted inputs, decompression, recursion, memory, execution time, concurrency and generated output sizes.
Preserve units, precision, ordering, provenance and compatibility when quantizing, translating, aggregating or serializing data.
Make automation idempotent and least-privileged; destructive or privileged operations require explicit authorization and rollback.
Treat decompilation and inspection as read-only; never execute untrusted source, packages, binaries or generated payloads.
Base performance and scaling claims on reproducible measurements with hardware, workload and environment context.
Allow not_applicable when a technique conflicts with the repository's product boundary or safety model.

execution_directives.intent: Define a complete capability slice, its owners, public boundaries and acceptance conditions before parallel implementation begins.
acceptance: Every new capability has a documented input, output, owner and explicit maturity status.
The implementation is connected to a real product path and covered by focused positive, boundary and failure tests.

execution_directives.intent: Design independent capabilities in parallel from one shared baseline, dependency map and set of compatibility assumptions.
acceptance: Parallel workstreams publish compatible interfaces and a dependency map before integration.
Conflicting changes to the same contract or mutable state are serialized and reviewed.

execution_directives.intent: Deliver the supporting tools needed to build, inspect, validate, diagnose and exercise the capability without creating unrelated tooling.
acceptance: Each tool has a bounded input contract, predictable output and actionable error behavior.
Tools are exercised by automated tests or a reproducible repository command.

execution_directives.intent: Provide the complete practical setup for a feature, including configuration, dependencies, build integration, fixtures and operator guidance.
acceptance: Required dependencies and configuration are declared with safe defaults and version constraints.
A clean checkout can follow the documented steps without undocumented manual setup.

execution_directives.intent: Wire each accepted component into its intended runtime or workflow and expose its supported lifecycle and failure states.
acceptance: No shipped component is an orphaned stub presented as an active capability.
Startup, normal operation, unavailable dependency and shutdown paths are tested where applicable.

execution_directives.intent: Reuse mature repository capabilities through explicit adapters and versioned contracts instead of duplicating logic or coupling internals.
acceptance: Every cross-module or cross-project integration names its provider, consumer, version and failure behavior.
Integration tests verify data shape, provenance and compatibility at the boundary.

execution_directives.intent: Modernize existing connections incrementally while preserving supported behavior and providing an explicit migration path.
acceptance: Existing public interfaces have compatibility tests or a documented versioned migration.
New dependencies and transport changes are justified, pinned or constrained, and reversible.

execution_directives.intent: Optimize measured bottlenecks only after recording a baseline and selecting a reference implementation or invariant.
acceptance: Performance changes include reproducible workload, environment and before/after measurements.
Optimized paths preserve reference semantics and pass regression, boundary and resource-limit tests.

execution_directives.intent: Automate independent repeatable operations with idempotent jobs, least privilege and explicit cancellation and retry limits.
acceptance: Repeated execution is safe and does not duplicate or corrupt side effects.
Automation has bounded retries, observable results and a documented recovery path.

execution_directives.intent: Improve command-line, build, test and diagnostic tools as one coherent developer workflow with consistent conventions.
acceptance: Related tools share documented naming, configuration and error-reporting conventions.
The complete tool workflow is covered by tests or a single reproducible verification command.

execution_directives.intent: Refactor components by responsibility and ownership while preserving their public contract and separating failure domains.
acceptance: Changed components have explicit inputs, outputs, resource limits and dependency direction.
Compatibility or migration tests show that supported callers retain the required behavior.

execution_directives.intent: Scale modules through stable extension points, bounded resource budgets and measured capacity rather than uncontrolled feature duplication.
acceptance: Module count, workload size and resource use have documented limits or capacity assumptions.
Independent modules can be tested and extended without bypassing shared contracts.

execution_directives.intent: Adapt implementations in coherent batches using platform-specific adapters and schema-validated configuration without changing canonical semantics.
acceptance: Each supported platform or format has an explicit capability check and fallback behavior.
Batch changes preserve deterministic ordering, provenance and version compatibility.

execution_directives.intent: Centralize shared automation rules and reusable scripts while leaving project-specific behavior behind clear adapters.
acceptance: There is one canonical source for shared rules and duplicate logic is removed or explicitly justified.
Shared automation is versioned, idempotent and independently testable.

execution_directives.intent: Coordinate optimization across connected components while defining ordering, consistency, conflict handling and rollback boundaries.
acceptance: Cross-component updates declare ordering, consistency and partial-failure behavior.
Combined changes are tested together and do not silently invalidate another repository's contract.

execution_directives.intent: Automate compatibility checks through explicit version, platform, architecture and schema matrices rather than guessing compatibility.
acceptance: Compatibility claims are tied to a named version/platform matrix and executable checks.
Unsupported combinations fail clearly; automated tooling never installs, flashes or mutates hardware without explicit authorization.

execution_directives.intent: Extend performance across related paths using shared measurement units, reference outputs and regression budgets.
acceptance: Benchmarks identify hardware, build mode, workload, units and measurement method.
Performance work is accepted only when correctness remains intact and regressions stay within a declared budget.

execution_directives.intent: Increase capacity through staged changes with observable thresholds, bounded resource use and a tested fallback or rollback.
acceptance: Scaling steps have measurable targets and resource ceilings.
Each stage passes the relevant load, reliability and rollback checks before the next stage is adopted.

execution_directives.intent: Improve portability and long-term usefulness through backward-compatible evolution, explicit uncertainty and supported-platform evidence.
acceptance: Platform-specific behavior is isolated behind documented interfaces and tested where CI supports it.
Continuous delivery remains compatible; disruptive migrations use staged rollout and a recovery path rather than bypassing checks.

execution_directives.intent: Make coordinated extensibility refactors behind stable contracts, with small reviewable changes and compatibility coverage.
acceptance: Extension points are explicit, versioned and covered by contract tests.
The refactor is split by dependency order; no unverified all-at-once rewrite is merged directly into the release path.
